paper.title: Tsallis-INF: An Optimal Algorithm for Stochastic and Adversarial Bandits

unmapped: regret measured as pseudo-regret against best arm in expectation, even for adaptive adversaries
settings.definition_quote: In the (\emph{adaptive}) \emph{adversarial setting}, the adversary selects the losses arbitrarily, potentially based on the history of the agent's actions $(\MyArm[1],\dots,\MyArm[t-1])$ and the adversary's own internal randomization.

settings.name_in_paper: adversarial regime with a (Delta, C, T) self-bounding constraint (unique zero entry)
settings.definition_quote: We further define an \emph{adversarial regime with a $(\Delta, C, T)$ self-bounding constraint}, where $\Delta\in[0,1]^K$ and $C\geq 0$. In this regime, the adversary selects losses such that at time $T$ the regret of any algorithm satisfies $\Reg \geq \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_i \Delta_i \mathbb{P}(I_t = i) - C$.

settings.name_in_paper: stochastically constrained adversarial regime with a unique best arm (gap-tuned regularizer)
unmapped: stochastically constrained adversary (fixed gaps, C=0 special case of self-bounding)
learner knows all gaps Delta_i to tune the asymmetric regularizer
settings.definition_quote: In this setting, the losses $\ell_{t,i}$ are drawn from distributions with fixed gaps, $\E[\ell_{t,i} - \ell_{t,j}] = \tilde \Delta_{i,j}$ independently of $t$, but the means, as well as other parameters of the distributions of all arms, are allowed to change with time and may depend on the agent's past actions

settings.name_in_paper: stochastically constrained adversarial environment with adversarial corruptions
unmapped: stochastically constrained adversary (unique best arm before corruption) adaptively corrupted with total corruption budget C (sum_t ||bar l_t - l_t||_inf <= C); generalizes stochastic_corrupted
settings.definition_quote: Let $\overline{\mathcal{L}}_T$ be a sequence of losses generated by a stochastically constrained adversary with best arm $i^*$ and gaps $\AnyGap$, and let $\mathcal{L}_T$ be its adaptively corrupted version with corruption amount bounded by $C$.

unmapped: utility-based dueling: P[W_t = I_t] = (1+u_{I_t}-u_{J_t})/2, regret 2u* - u_{I_t} - u_{J_t}
settings.definition_quote: The problem is defined by $K$ arms with utilities $u_i\in [0,1]$. At each round, an agent has to select two arms ... The feedback is the winner $W_t$ of the ``duel'', which is chosen according to $\mathbb{P}[W_t=\MyArm[t]] = \frac{1+u_{\MyArm[t]}-u_{\OtherArm[t]}}{2}$.

unmapped: utilities u_{t,i} chosen by adversary; regret vs best utility in hindsight
settings.definition_quote: In the adversarial version of the problem, the utilities $u_i$ are not constant but time dependent, $u_{t,i}$, and selected by an adversary.

_verify.summary: The extraction is accurate and complete. All bounds from Theorems 1, 3 and 4 and Corollaries 8 and 10 are recorded with the correct constants, regimes and settings, and the algorithm registry ids match. The only blemish is the note on r2, which says the proof gives 28K log T when the adversarial-branch derivation actually gives 14K log T; the recorded expression is still correct as stated.
